page.description: Qubes OS 4.3.2 ISO: architecture, size and the mirror's DIGESTS file.
page.intro: A desktop that separates work into isolated virtual machines called qubes. It is installed like a normal system, but assumes a hostile environment and a trusted screen.
pros: Compartmentalisation by default: apps run in separate qubes.
Templates keep the base system shared and updateable.
Security-first design with a documented threat model.
One x86_64 ISO covers the install.
cons: Needs hardware with VT-x/AMD-V, VT-d and enough RAM (16 GB is realistic).
The workflow is different from a normal desktop.
The Commons screenshot is older than 4.3.2.
page.previewNote: A stock screenshot of a Qubes OS desktop from Wikimedia Commons. It is not 4.3.2 and not a ROMinit recording: no image was written and nothing was booted for this page.

page.status: One image: the x86_64 ISO, written with dd or any image writer. Writing erases the stick; the installer then partitions or erases the target disk. The date shown is the mirror file date; Qubes publishes no separate release date on this page.
